adds.title: Montana Senate Bill 437 (2026) - definitions of gender, male, female, man, woman, mother, father
adds.summary: On March 24, 2026 Montana enacted Senate Bill 437 defining sex as binary male or female based on primary sexual anatomy and reproductive system (female as ova-based, male as sperm-based), defining man, woman, mother and father on that basis and providing that gender means that sex definition and not gender identity, experienced gender, expression or role, with the definitions applying in 60+ sections of state law including driver's licenses, marriage licenses and anti-discrimination protections, requiring applicants for driver's and marriage licenses to list sex as so defined.

adds.title: Montana birth certificate and driver's license gender-marker restrictions and injunctions
adds.summary: In December 2024 a Helena district court preliminarily enjoined Montana from enforcing its 2022 health department rule barring gender-identity-based changes to birth-certificate sex, its Motor Vehicle Division policy requiring a birth certificate to change driver's-license sex, and portions of 2023 Senate Bill 458 defining male/female by reproductive biology, finding plaintiffs likely to succeed on claims that the restrictions constitute sex discrimination violating the Montana Constitution's fundamental right to be free from sex discrimination and pausing enforcement while litigation continues.

adds.title: Montana House Bill 819 (May 2025) - government flag 'neutrality' law
adds.summary: Montana House Bill 819, debated March 6, 2025 and signed by Gov. Greg Gianforte in May 2025 with immediate effect, prohibits flags representing political party, race, sexual orientation, gender or political ideology on government property and public schools, thereby banning Pride and other LGBTQ flags, while permitting official historical flags including the Gadsden flag, law-enforcement/Thin Blue Line flags, tribal nation, foreign country, military service branch, POW/MIA, and official school or government entity flags.
